title: Cutting EBS, EFS, FSx & Log Storage Costs
summary: Cheaper volume types, snapshot archiving, file system tiering and log retention.
tldr: **EBS:** move gp2 to **gp3** in place with Elastic Volumes (cheaper per GB, performance set independently of size). Large sequential reads go to **st1**; rarely read sequential data goes to **sc1**.
**Snapshots and backups:** archive long-kept EBS snapshots to **EBS Snapshots Archive** with Data Lifecycle Manager, and move long-retention AWS Backup recovery points to **cold storage**.

**File systems tier themselves:** EFS lifecycle to **Infrequent Access** and **Archive**, FSx for ONTAP **capacity pool** with a tiering policy, FSx for Windows **HDD + deduplication**. Same mount path, no data moves by hand.
**Logs:** set retention instead of *Never expire*, use the CloudWatch Logs **Infrequent Access** class for rarely queried logs, and use OpenSearch **UltraWarm / cold** tiers with ISM policies.

keyFacts.text: gp3 baseline at any size, with IOPS and throughput provisioned separately. Usually cheaper than gp2 or io2 when needs are moderate.
EBS Snapshots Archive storage cost versus standard tier. Minimum 90 days archived; restoring can take up to 72 hours.
Maximum throughput of st1 versus sc1. Both are HDD, can't be boot volumes, and suit large sequential I/O only.
EFS lifecycle moves files by days since last access, and can move them back to Standard on first access. Namespace and Multi-AZ stay unchanged.
RDS grows allocated storage automatically up to a maximum threshold, so you can start small instead of paying for years of headroom.

traps: EBS snapshots are not in a bucket you own, so S3 Lifecycle rules can't archive them; use Data Lifecycle Manager or the archive API.
Increasing a gp3 volume's size doesn't raise its throughput; provision throughput directly with Elastic Volumes.
EFS One Zone or FSx Single-AZ cuts cost but breaks any requirement to stay Multi-AZ.
Unattached EBS volumes keep billing; snapshot them, delete them, and set `DeleteOnTermination` to true in launch templates.
Moving cold files out of a file system to S3 Glacier breaks the requirement to open them through the same mount path.
